name: Jass (Schieber)
description: Jass is the national card game of Switzerland, specifically the 'Schieber' variant, which is a four-player partnership trick-taking game. It features a unique 36-card deck (Acorns, Bells, Shields, Flowers) and a complex point-tracking system. The game is highly strategic, requiring players to deduce their partner's strength through 'pushing' the trump selection and careful card signaling.

overview.description: Jass is the national card game of Switzerland, specifically the 'Schieber' variant, which is a four-player partnership trick-taking game. It features a unique 36-card deck (Acorns, Bells, Shields, Flowers) and a complex point-tracking system. The game is highly strategic, requiring players to deduce their partner's strength through 'pushing' the trump selection and careful card signaling.

history.origins: Part of the 'Marriage' family of games (related to Marias and Belote). It emerged in Switzerland in the 18th century and evolved into various regional forms. The 'Schieber' (Pushing) variant became the dominant nationalist form in the 20th century.
timeline: 1790s: First mention of 'Jass' in Swiss military records.
1900s: Jass decks with Swiss-German suits (Acorns/Bells) become standardized.
1960s: Jass becomes a televised phenomenon in Switzerland (Samschtig-Jass).
Present: An integral part of Swiss social identity, played by millions.
history.cultural: Used at every social level in Switzerland; a common way for neighbors to bond in local taverns (Beizen).
history.evolution: The game's point values (especially the 'Puur' and 'NÃ¤ll' in trumps) create a distinct hierarchy that differs from standard French-suited games.

setup.deck:
36 cards: A, K, O (Queen), U (Jack), 10, 9, 8, 7, 6.
**Cards vary by suit color**: German-Swiss (Acorns, Bells, Roses, Shields) or French (Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, Spades).
setup.dealing: Dealer deals 9 cards to each player (in batches of 3).

rules.objective: Score a target number of points (usually 1000 or 2500) through trick-taking and melds (Weis).
rules.gameplay:
1. Must follow suit. If unable, you can trump or discard.
2. **StÃ¶ck**: Holding the King and Ober of the trump suit (20 pts).
3. **Weis**: Melds declared during the first trick (e.g., four of a kind, sequences).
keyRules: Must follow suit if possible; may trump or discard if unable. When trumping, must overtrump if holding a higher trump.
Puur (trump Jack) need not be played when it is the only trump in hand.
Eldest (right of dealer) leads to the first trick; winner of each trick leads next.
Stöck (King and Ober of trumps) scores 20 when claimed on playing the second card to a trick.
Weis (melds) are declared when contributing to the first trick; only the best meld scores.

strategy.basic: Prioritize high-value trumps (Puur and NÃ¤ll). Always try to win the last trick for the bonus points. Learn to recognize your partner's 'signaling' through their discards.
strategy.intermediate: The Push: If you have a mediocre hand, 'push' to your partner. If you have a solid suit (even if not 'pure' trumps), select it and lead aggressively.
strategy.advanced: Undenufe/Obenabe mastery: These no-trump variants can score much higher points if you correctly identify that your hand is strong in 'Low' or 'High' cards respectively.
tips: Don't lead your trump Puur (Under) unless you are trying to bleed the opponent's NÃ¤ll (9).
Count the points! Knowing that 157 is the total helps you gauge how close you are to the win.

variations.name: Obenabe
variations.description: No trump; cards rank Ace high to Six low; eights count 8 points each so pack totals 157. Points often multiplied by three.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: No-trump variant; overrides would need trumpConfig and rank changes; base engine covers flow.

variations.name: Undenufe
variations.description: No trump; suits inverted (6 highest, Ace lowest). Eights count 8 points each. Points often multiplied by four.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Inverted ranking variant; overrides would need trumpConfig and rank order; base engine covers flow.

variations.name: Match and counter-match
variations.description: Team taking all nine tricks scores 257 (157 + 100 match bonus). If the team that did not choose trump takes every trick, their points are doubled (counter-match).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Score bonus rules only; no engine constant overrides needed for implementation.

variations.name: Schilten/Schellen double
variations.description: Scores in Shields (Schilten) or Bells (Schellen) as trump are doubled; target may be raised to 2500 or 3000.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Score multiplier and target changes; would need constants.targetScore and multiplier if added.

scoring.description: Score a target number of points (usually 1000 or 2500) through trick-taking and melds (Weis).
scoring.winCondition: First team to reach the agreed target (typically 2500 points) wins.
